reconcile.connective: Keil & Delitzsch concede the biology but argue Moses spoke in the popular idiom, describing how the animals appear to chew rather than true anatomy.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells presses the same point empirically: hares and coneys are not ruminants and simply do not chew the cud, whatever the text claims.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, Leviticus 11 ("Science" note on the hare and coney)
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (2013; online edition skepticsannotatedbible.com/lev/11.html), noting hares and coneys 'are not ruminants and they do not chew the cud'

excerpts.excerpt_text: It is true that modern naturalists affirm that the two latter do not ruminate at all, as they have not the four stomachs that are common to ruminant animals; but they move the jaw sometimes in a manner which looks like ruminating, so that even Linnaeus affirmed that the hare chewed the cud, and Moses followed the popular opinion.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: K&D concede directly, in their own words, that modern naturalists deny hares/hyraxes truly ruminate (no four-chambered stomach), then explain the text via phenomenological/popular language rather than technical zoology -- the single strongest, most explicit harmonization on this row, and it comes from a block-anchored note whose on-tension sentence sits deep in a general discussion of Lev 11:4-8.

pd_work.resource: Keil & Delitzsch, Biblical Commentary on the Old Testament (1861-75), on Leviticus 11:4-6
pd_work.author: Keil & Delitzsch
pd_work.note: K&D treat this exact passage directly, conceding that modern naturalists deny hares/hyraxes truly ruminate while defending Moses' wording as following 'popular opinion.' Used as the PD anchor because Haley's Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874 text, checked by full-text search for 'cud', 'ruminant', 'hare', 'coney', 'Leviticus xi') has no dedicated treatment of this passage; K&D is a harmonizing commentator already surfaced on the row and keyed to the exact verse.

link.title: Is there a Bible contradiction in Leviticus 11:5-6?
